To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
creatine kinase, bound to the myofilaments of the taenia, is capable of generating ATP and relaxing rigor tension.

creatine kinase (an enzyme that transfers a phosphate from phosphocreatine (PCr) to ADP to make ATP) is associated with the contractile proteins in the smooth muscle of guinea pig taenias coli, and that this association is important for tension generation in smooth muscle.
creatine kinase, associated with the contractile apparatus of the taenia colii, plays a role in the regulation of tension generation in this muscle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the myofibrillar bound creatine kinase (MBCK) in the contractile process.
the role of creatine phosphokinase (CK) in the contractile process of smooth muscle and with the possible role of CK associated with the contractile proteins in the regulation of ATPase activity.
the role of creatine kinases in muscle and their possible involvement in the compartmentation and utilization of adenine nucleotide.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
creatine kinase is an integral part of the contractile mechanism and is associated with the myosin filaments.
the BB isoform of creatine kinase is localized to the myofibers of the taenia and that the enzyme is involved in the maintenance of the ATP/ADP ratio in smooth muscle.

creatine kinase plays a role in smooth muscle relaxation, and that the role of creatine phosphokinase in muscle is not limited to the production of ATP for contraction, but may be involved in other aspects of muscle function, such as relaxation and maintenance of the rigor state.
